citations.quote:
Let $C\ge1$ be the number of components and $P\ge1$ the number of phases. Use common positive real coordinates $T,p$, expressed in fixed units if they are given a physical interpretation, and, for each phase $\alpha$, an interior composition vector

$$x^\alpha\in\Omega_C:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{C-1}:x_i>0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{C-1}x_i<1\},$$

with the convention $\mathbb R^0=\{0\}$ and $\Omega_1=\{0\}$. The final component fraction is $1-\sum_{i<C}x_i>0$. The ambient coordinate domain $U=(0,\infty)^2\times\Omega_C^P$ is open in $\mathbb R^n$, where $n=2+P(C-1)$. For each phase $\alpha$ and component $i$, let $\mu_i^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)$ be a real-valued $C^1$ coordinate function; these are mathematical maps and no thermodynamic potential or physical realization is assumed.

For $P\ge2$, define the $q=C(P-1)$ coexistence equations

$$F_{i,\alpha}(T,p,x^1,\ldots,x^P)=\mu_i^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)-\mu_i^1(T,p,x^1)=0\quad(1\le i\le C,\ 2\le\alpha\le P).$$

At a solution $z_*\in U$, assume some $q\times q$ derivative minor of $F:U\to\mathbb R^q$ is invertible. Then the local solution set is a graph of dimension

$$n-q=2+P(C-1)-C(P-1)=C-P+2.$$

For $P=1$ there are no coexistence equations and the coordinate domain itself has dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2$. In a specified reactive variant with $R\ge1$, let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent dimensionless stoichiometric vectors and add the $R$ affinity equations $A_r=\sum_{i=1}^C\nu_i^r\mu_i^1=0$. If the combined equation map has an invertible $(q+R)\times(q+R)$ derivative minor at a solution and $q+R\le n$, its local zero set has dimension

$$n-q-R=C-P+2-R.$$

These are conditional local dimensions under the displayed nonsingular-minor assumptions. No dimension formula follows at singular solutions, on composition boundaries, or from equation counting alone; no empirical or general physical phase rule is asserted.

Fix a material constitution $c$, with $r$ named species and dimensionless equilibrium state domain $D_c\subseteq\mathbb R^{r+2}$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in D_c$, define the diagonal SI coordinate map

$$\Phi_c(x):=(U_c(x),V_c(x),n_{c,1}(x),\ldots,n_{c,r}(x))=(\hat U\,\mathrm J,\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3},\hat n_1\,\mathrm{mol},\ldots,\hat n_r\,\mathrm{mol}).$$

In SI numerical coordinates this is a diagonal linear bijection with a diagonal linear inverse, so it maps ambient open sets to open sets and its inverse is defined on its image.

Choose an open subset $O\subseteq D_c$ in the ambient dimensionless Euclidean coordinates that is designated as a single-phase chart, and set $\Omega:=\Phi_c(O)$, an open chart of physical SI coordinate values. Here $U$ is the internal-energy coordinate evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame of [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. If $S_c:D_c\to\mathbb R$ is the entropy adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], define its physical-coordinate representative on $\Omega$ by

$$S_c^{\mathrm{SI}}:=S_c\circ\Phi_c^{-1}:\Omega\to\mathbb R.$$

When its arguments are the physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, write this representative as $S_c(U,V,n)$ for brevity. On $\Omega$, assume the finite representative is $C^2$ and has $S_{c,U}>0$, as adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Here $C^2$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through order two exist and are continuous ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A coordinate partial such as $S_{c,U}$ is the ordinary derivative in the physical $U$ coordinate while every other physical coordinate is held fixed, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; in particular the conversion factor from $\hat U$ is included.

Explicitly, with the partial derivatives on the right taken in the dimensionless coordinates on $O$ while holding every other hatted coordinate fixed, the physical partials are

$$S_{c,U}^{\mathrm{SI}}=(1\,\mathrm J)^{-1}\partial_{\hat U}S_c,\qquad S_{c,V}^{\mathrm{SI}}=(1\,\mathrm{m^3})^{-1}\partial_{\hat V}S_c,\qquad S_{c,n_j}^{\mathrm{SI}}=(1\,\mathrm{mol})^{-1}\partial_{\hat n_j}S_c,$$

using the coordinate-conversion convention of [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]].

Define the physical-coordinate representatives of the **absolute thermodynamic temperature**, **entropic pressure**, and **molar chemical potential** of species $j$ by

$$T_c^{\mathrm{SI}}:=\frac{1}{S_{c,U}^{\mathrm{SI}}},\qquad p_c^{\mathrm{SI}}:=T_c^{\mathrm{SI}}S_{c,V}^{\mathrm{SI}},\qquad \mu_{c,j}^{\mathrm{SI}}:=-T_c^{\mathrm{SI}}S_{c,n_j}^{\mathrm{SI}}.$$

For a state-domain point $x\in O$, define the corresponding state functions by pullback, $T_c(x):=T_c^{\mathrm{SI}}(\Phi_c(x))$, $p_c(x):=p_c^{\mathrm{SI}}(\Phi_c(x))$, and $\mu_{c,j}(x):=\mu_{c,j}^{\mathrm{SI}}(\Phi_c(x))$. When the argument is a physical tuple $(U,V,n)$, write $T_c(U,V,n)$, $p_c(U,V,n)$, and $\mu_{c,j}(U,V,n)$ for the physical-coordinate representatives. Thus both notations refer to the same state functions through $\Phi_c$.

The entropy unit is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the energy $U$ is in joules, $V$ is in cubic metres, and $n_j$ is in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Thus $S_{c,U}^{\mathrm{SI}}$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $T_c$ is finite and positive in kelvins, $S_{c,V}^{\mathrm{SI}}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ and $p_c$ has units pascals, and $S_{c,n_j}^{\mathrm{SI}}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\mu_{c,j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. If a microscopic model instead uses a dimensionless particle count $N_j=N_{\!A}n_j$, the corresponding per-particle chemical potential is $\mu_{c,j}/N_{\!A}$ joules, with the exact SI Avogadro constant from [[def-td-si-quantities]].

These are scalar state functions of the stated rest-frame equilibrium chart. The pressure in this definition is a derivative-defined conjugate; identifying it with force per area requires a separate adopted mechanical coupling. Neither an empirical thermometer calibration nor any equation of state is supplied by this definition.

Assume the entropy of each phase is $C^2$ on its physical state chart and its derivative-defined temperature at the endpoint is finite and positive. The equation-set dimension below concerns this smooth interior state only.

Let $C\ge1$ be the number of named species, $P\ge1$ the number of coexisting phase branches, and $R\ge0$ the number of independent internal reaction directions. Consider an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For each phase $\alpha$, use an intensive phase branch from [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] and an interior composition $x^\alpha\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}$. Let each branch chemical-potential map
$$
\mu^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)=(\mu_1^\alpha,\ldots,\mu_C^\alpha)
$$
be $C^1$ on a common open domain
$$
\mathcal U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ})^P \subseteq\mathbb R^{\,n},\qquad n=2+P(C-1).
$$
Assume energy, volume, and every named species can be exchanged between every phase pair in both directions, and every listed reaction direction is feasible in both extent directions in every phase while that phase's energy, volume, other reaction extents, and all other phase coordinates are held fixed at the coexistence point. Let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent, dimensionless stoichiometric vectors, with extents measured in moles. Phase equilibrium imposes $\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1=0$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$; internal reaction equilibrium imposes $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase for $1\le r\le R$. On the phase-equality locus these are the same $R$ equations in each phase, so count them once using phase 1. Put $q:=C(P-1)$ and $m:=q+R$. If $m=0$ (equivalently $P=1,R=0$), no equation is imposed and the local zero set is the whole chart, of dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2-R$. If $m\ge1$ and the combined equation map has an invertible $m\times m$ derivative minor at the solution, with $m\le n$, then the local zero set of these first-order coexistence-and-affinity equations is a graph of dimension
$$
n-q-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This is the dimension of the equation zero set in intensive coordinates only; phase amounts and their extensive conservation constraints are not counted, and the actual stable-coexistence set may be a proper subset after additional stability constraints. If the nonsingular-minor condition fails, no dimension formula is asserted.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

derivations.claim: Differentiating the conjugate assignments in [A1] gives $dG=-S\,dT+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$; differentiating $U=G+TS-pV$ gives $dU=T\,dS-p\,dV+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$. Thus $S_U=1/T$, $S_V=p/T$, and $S_{n_j}=-\mu_j/T$, as in [F2]. From the displayed $g^\gamma$, at the center $S_T=m_\gamma c/T_0$, $U_T=m_\gamma c$, $V_T=0$, and $V_p=-m_\gamma\kappa$, so the fixed-composition/amount $(T,p)$ Jacobian for $(U,V)$ is $-m_\gamma^2c\kappa$. The map $(x_1,x_2,m_\gamma)\mapsto(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ has determinant $m_\gamma^2(x_1+x_2+x_3)=m_\gamma^2$. Hence the full state-map Jacobian is $-m_\gamma^4c\kappa\ne0$, and [L2] gives a local physical state chart.

For $m=n_1+n_2+n_3$ and $x_j=n_j/m$, [L1] at fixed $T,p$ and the other two species amounts gives
$$
\mu_1=g+(1-x_1)g_{x_1}-x_2g_{x_2},\quad \mu_2=g-x_1g_{x_1}+(1-x_2)g_{x_2},\quad \mu_3=g-x_1g_{x_1}-x_2g_{x_2}.
$$
Substitution of the two stated $g^\gamma$ at the centered point gives $\mu^\alpha=\mu^\beta=(0,0,0)$. Thus $F_i=\mu_i^\beta-\mu_i^\alpha=0$ and $A=\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$.

In columns $(x_1^\beta,x_2^\beta,p,x_1^\alpha)$, the derivative minor of $(F_1,F_2,F_3,A)$ at the centered point is
$$
\begin{pmatrix} 2\eta/3&-\eta/3&0&0\\ -\eta/3&2\eta/3&0&0\\ -\eta/3&-\eta/3&q&0\\ 0&0&0&-5a_\alpha/6 \end{pmatrix}.
$$
It is nonsingular: the upper-left $2\times2$ block has determinant $\eta^2/3\ne0$, and the remaining diagonal factors are $q>0$ and $-5a_\alpha/6\ne0$. The combined equation map therefore has the required rank four.

The ambient coordinate dimension is $n=2+P(C-1)=6$, and the number of equations is $q+R=C(P-1)+R=3+1=4$. By [F1], the local equation zero set has dimension $6-4=2$, agreeing with $C-P+2-R=3-2+2-1=2$. This is only the full-rank equation-set calculation.

Take $C=3$ species and $P=2$ phases. Write $x_3:=1-x_1-x_2$, and center the open composition charts at $x_1=x_2=x_3=1/3$. Fix $T_0>0$, $p_0>0$, $s_0,c,v_0,\kappa,q>0$, and $\eta=1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. The parameters have units $s_0,c\in\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $v_0\in\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, $\kappa\in\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}Pa^{-1}}$, and $q\in\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$. For $\gamma\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, set $a_\alpha=2\eta$, $a_\beta=\eta$, $q_\alpha=0$, and $q_\beta=q$, and define molar Gibbs potentials
$$
g^\gamma(T,p,x)=-s_0(T-T_0)-\frac{c}{2T_0}(T-T_0)^2+v_0(p-p_0)-\frac{\kappa}{2}(p-p_0)^2+\frac{a_\gamma}{2}(x_1^2+x_2^2)-\frac{a_\gamma}{3}(x_1+x_2)+\frac{a_\gamma}{9}+q_\gamma(p-p_0)x_3.
$$
Set $G^\gamma=m_\gamma g^\gamma$ on each fixed-tag branch and adopt the natural Gibbs assignments $S=-G_T$, $V=G_p$, and $\mu_j=G_{n_j}$, with $U=G+TS-pV$. These smooth charts are scale-invariant in amount. Near the centered point the volumes are positive, and the $(U,V)$ chart Jacobian at fixed composition and amount is nonsingular: $U_T=m_\gamma c$, $V_p=-m_\gamma\kappa$, and $V_T=0$ there, so its determinant is $-m_\gamma^2c\kappa\ne0$. The reaction vector is $\nu=(-1,-1/2,1)^{\mathsf T}$, of rank $R=1$. At $(T_0,p_0,x_1,x_2)=(T_0,p_0,1/3,1/3)$, both phases have $\mu^\gamma=(0,0,0)$, so the phase-equality equations and reaction affinity vanish.

The constructed branch's local physical state map is $\chi:(T,p,n)\mapsto(U,V,n)$ (using the positive amount and interior composition coordinates displayed here). On the inverse patch verified below, define its numerical domain $O_c=\Phi_c^{-1}(\chi(\mathcal O))$ and declare this patch to be the local model's $D_c$ patch, where $\Phi_c(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=(\hat U\,\mathrm J,\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3},\hat n\,\mathrm{mol})$ is the unit map of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Define the numerical entropy by $S_c=S^{\rm SI}\circ\Phi_c$, with $S^{\rm SI}$ supplied by the Gibbs assignments through this inverse. Thus the displayed derivatives are derivatives in physical SI coordinates on $\Phi_c(O_c)$; the model patch is not an empirical claim about an independently specified material domain.

citations.quote:
Fix $C\ge1$ species and $R\ge1$ declared internal reaction extents. Let $\nu\in\mathbb R^{C\times R}$ be the dimensionless stoichiometric matrix, let $n^0\in[0,\infty)^C$ have units mol, and let $\xi\in\mathbb R^R$ have units mol. The amount vector is $n(\xi)=n^0+\nu\xi$, and the nonnegative-amount feasible extent set is
$$
\mathcal F_\nu:=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^R:n^0+\nu\xi\in[0,\infty)^C\}.
$$
Fix $T_0>0$ and $p_0$ in a declared natural-variable chart. Let $\Phi(\xi)$ be the constrained Gibbs potential on an open neighborhood $U$ of an equilibrium extent $\xi_*$, and assume the model supplies a finite $C^1$ extension through every zero-amount boundary point under consideration. On $U$, assume
$$
D\Phi(\xi)[h]=\sum_{j=1}^C\mu_j(\xi)(\nu h)_j=(\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu(\xi))\cdot h,
$$
where $\mu_j$ are the molar chemical potentials in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. This extension and derivative identity are not supplied by the positive-mole phase chart itself.

Suppose $\xi_*$ is an attained stable equilibrium for the fixed-$T_0,p_0$ internal reaction model with the ideal reservoirs of [[pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-minimum]]. Then $\xi_*$ minimizes $\Phi$ on the exact reaction-feasible set locally. Let $J_*:=\{j:n^0_j+(\nu\xi_*)_j=0\}$ be the active species set. The feasible tangent cone is
$$
T_{\mathcal F_\nu}(\xi_*):=\{h\in\mathbb R^R:(\nu h)_j\ge0\text{ for every }j\in J_*\}.
$$
The first-order necessary condition is
$$
(\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu(\xi_*))\cdot h\ge0\qquad(h\in T_{\mathcal F_\nu}(\xi_*)).
$$
If $\xi_*$ is interior to $\mathcal F_\nu$, this reduces to $\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu(\xi_*)=0$. If, in addition, $\Phi$ is convex and differentiable on a convex neighborhood containing the relevant feasible set, the same tangent inequality is sufficient for global minimization there.

derivations.claim:
Here species $A$ is active because $n_A(\xi_*)=0$. A tangent extent $h$ must satisfy $(
u h)_A=-h\ge0$, so $h\le0$. The affinity vector is the scalar $
u^{\mathsf T}\mu=-\mu_A+\mu_B=-1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. Hence $(
u^{\mathsf T}\mu)h\ge0$ for every feasible tangent extent $h\le0$.

Directly, $\Phi(\xi)-\Phi(0)=-(1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}})\xi\ge0$ for every feasible $\xi\in[-1,0]$ mol, so the boundary point is a global minimum on this interval. It need not satisfy the interior equality $\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu=0$.

Use species $A,B$, one reaction column $\nu=(-1,1)^{\mathsf T}$, and starting amounts $n_A^0=0$ mol, $n_B^0=1$ mol. The admissible extents are $\xi\in[-1,0]$ mol because $n_A(\xi)=-\xi$ and $n_B(\xi)=1\,\mathrm{mol}+\xi$ must both be nonnegative. Let $\Phi_0$ have units joules and define an ambient affine potential on an open neighborhood of the nonnegative amount region by
$$
\widehat\Phi(n_A,n_B)=\Phi_0+1\,\mathrm J-(1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}})n_B .
$$
Along $n(\xi)=(-\xi,1\,\mathrm{mol}+\xi)$, set $\Phi(\xi):=\widehat\Phi(n(\xi))=\Phi_0-(1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}})\xi$. Its derivative-defined amount coefficients are $\mu_A:=\partial_{n_A}\widehat\Phi=0$ and $\mu_B:=\partial_{n_B}\widehat\Phi=-1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, including at $\xi_*=0$ mol. This ambient extension is constructed optimization data only; no positive-mole thermodynamic chart at $n_A=0$ or physical realization is asserted.

derivations.claim:
At fixed $t$, differentiating the rational equation gives
$$
\frac{\partial p}{\partial v}=-\frac{24t}{(3v-1)^2}+\frac{6}{v^3}.
$$
At $t=0.9$ and $v=1$, this derivative is $-24(0.9)/4+6=0.6>0$.

The second derivative is $\partial_v^2p=144t/(3v-1)^3-18/v^4$. At a simultaneous zero, the first derivative gives $t=(3v-1)^2/(4v^3)$ and the second gives $t=(3v-1)^3/(8v^4)$. Equality and $v>1/3$ imply $2v=3v-1$, hence $v=1$, $t=1$, and $p=1$. Conversely these values make both derivatives zero. Thus $T_c$ is the model critical temperature in this stated sense, and $t=0.9<1$ is below it.

The derivative is continuous near $(t,v)=(0.9,1)$ because $3v-1\ne0$ there. Hence it remains positive on some open neighborhood within $v>1/3$. Since $P=P_cp$ and $V=V_cv$ with positive scales, $(\partial P/\partial V)_T=(P_c/V_c)(\partial p/\partial v)_t>0$ there as well. This verifies a positive-slope branch of this phenomenological model only.

case_scope.source_excerpt:
Adopt the reduced van der Waals equation as a phenomenological model:
$$
p(v,t)=\frac{8t}{3v-1}-\frac{3}{v^2},\qquad v>\frac13,\quad t>0,
$$
where $p=P/P_c$, $v=V/V_c$, and $t=T/T_c$ use positive model scales $P_c,V_c,T_c$. Define a model critical point by the simultaneous isothermal conditions $\partial_vp=\partial_v^2p=0$ in this domain. The equation is a model premise; its extension to liquid-like densities is not a universal physical law.

citations.quote:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty compact set of dimensionless generator coordinates. Each $x\in K$ labels one model-specified phase-generator state; the model assigns it entropy per mole $s(x)\in\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $s:K\to\mathbb R$ is continuous, using the numerical entropy value in that fixed unit. Define $\operatorname{conv}K$ to be the set of all finite convex combinations of points of $K$, and fix $\bar x\in\operatorname{conv}K$. Use the Borel sigma algebra relative to $K$. A Borel probability mixture is a countably additive probability measure $P$ on that sigma algebra; its barycenter and entropy per mole are the coordinatewise integrals $\int_Kx\,dP$ and $\int_Ks\,dP$. For $x\in K$, define the unit point mass $\delta_x$ by $\delta_x(A)=1$ if $x\in A$ and $\delta_x(A)=0$ otherwise, for Borel $A\subseteq K$. Assume every Borel probability mixture with barycenter $\bar x$ is feasible and has entropy per mole $\int_Ks\,dP$. Then there are $m\le d+1$, points $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in K$, and weights $\theta_i\ge0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i=1$ such that $P_*:=\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i\delta_{x_i}$ is a feasible Borel probability mixture and $\int_Ks\,dP_*\ge\int_Ks\,dP$ for every feasible mixture $P$.

Here integrals use the measure convention of [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]. The entropy map is part of the model; this theorem derives neither its microscopic meaning nor compactness of a physical phase domain.

Let $(X,\mathcal T)$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]). The
**Borel sigma-algebra of $X$** is the sigma-algebra generated by its open sets:

$$\mathcal B(X):=\sigma_X(\mathcal T).$$

Its members are the **Borel subsets** of $X$. The generated sigma-algebra exists
and is minimal by [[thm-generated-sigma-algebra-exists-and-is-minimal]].

A **probability measure** on a measurable space $(X,\mathcal A)$ is a measure $\mathbb P$ with $\mathbb P(X)=1$ ([[def-measure]]). The triple $(X,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)$ is a **probability space** ([[def-measure-space]]); $X$ is its sample space and the members of $\mathcal A$ are its events.

A measure space is a triple $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ where $\Sigma$ contains $\varnothing,X$ and is closed under complements and countable unions (a $\sigma$-algebra) of subsets of $X$ and $\mu:\Sigma\to[0,\infty]$ is countably additive with $\mu(\varnothing)=0$. A measurable function $f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]$ has measurable inverse images of Borel sets, where $[-\infty,\infty]$ has its order topology: finite open intervals and the endpoint neighborhoods $[-\infty,a)$ and $(a,\infty]$ form a basis. Its Borel sigma-algebra is generated by these open sets. A complex-valued function is measurable exactly when its finite real and imaginary parts are measurable, equivalently for the usual Borel structure of $\mathbb C$. Almost-everywhere assertions mean outside a measurable $\mu$-null set; completeness of $\mu$ is not assumed. Nonnegative extended addition uses $a+\infty=\infty+a=\infty$ for $a\in[0,\infty]$; positive scalars multiply $\infty$ to $\infty$, while $0\cdot\infty=0$. Signed expressions $\infty-\infty$ remain undefined and are not used in signed integrals. A nonnegative simple function has the form $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ with finitely many disjoint $A_j\in\Sigma$ and finite $c_j\ge0$. Define $c\mu(A)=+\infty$ if $c>0$ and $\mu(A)=+\infty$, define $0\cdot\infty:=0$, and define the finite sum of these extended nonnegative terms to be $+\infty$ if any term is $+\infty$ and otherwise the real finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]]. Then $\int s\,d\mu:=\sum_j c_j\mu(A_j)$; using canonical level sets $\{s=c\}$ makes this value representation-independent. For measurable $f\ge0$, define $\int f\,d\mu:=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: s\text{ is simple and }0\le s\le f\}$, using [[def-complete-ordered-field]] for a bounded set of finite values and setting the supremum to $+\infty$ when the values are unbounded or one is infinite. A real measurable $f$ is integrable when $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$, and then $\int f:=\int f^+-\int f^-$, where $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-:=\max(-f,0)$. Complex integrability and integration are defined by integrable real and imaginary parts.

derivations.claim:
Since $0< s_0-a\le s(x)\le s_0$, every feasible $s$ is nonnegative and bounded. For $n\ge2$, put $A_n:=\{x\in K:|x|\ge1/n\}$. Their union is $K$; since $P(K)=1$, countable additivity implies $P(A_n)>0$ for some $n$. On $A_n$, $s\le s_0-a/n$, and on its complement $s\le s_0$. For any nonnegative simple function $\varphi\le s$, the measure integral definition [F2] therefore gives
$$
\int_K\varphi\,dP\le (s_0-a/n)P(A_n)+s_0P(K\setminus A_n)=s_0-aP(A_n)/n<s_0.
$$
Indeed, refine the finitely many level sets of $\varphi$ by $A_n$ and its complement; each simple-function coefficient is bounded by the corresponding pointwise bound on that piece, so the simple-integral formula [F2] gives the inequality. The common strict upper bound is independent of $\varphi$, hence its supremum also satisfies $\int_Ks\,dP<s_0$.

For each $0<\epsilon<1$, the measure $P_\epsilon=\tfrac12\delta_{-\epsilon}+\tfrac12\delta_{\epsilon}$ is supported on $K$, has mean zero, and satisfies $\int s\,dP_\epsilon=s_0-a\epsilon$. Letting $\epsilon\downarrow0$ shows that the supremum is $s_0$. Step 1.1 shows that no feasible measure attains it. This lies outside the compactness hypothesis in [F1] and exhibits a finite supremum without a maximizing mixture.

case_scope.source_excerpt:
Let $K=(-1,0)\cup(0,1)$, which is noncompact: the open cover $U_n=(-1,-1/n)\cup(1/n,1)$ for $n\ge2$ has no finite subcover. Let $C=[-1,1]$ and use dimensionless coordinate $x$. For constants $s_0>a>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, define the ambient entropy extension and its restriction by
$$
\widetilde s(x)=s_0-a x^2\quad(x\in C),\qquad s=\widetilde s|_K.
$$
For $x,y\in C$ and $t\in[0,1]$,
$$
\widetilde s((1-t)x+ty)=(1-t)\widetilde s(x)+t\widetilde s(y)+a t(1-t)(x-y)^2\ge(1-t)\widetilde s(x)+t\widetilde s(y),
$$
so $\widetilde s$ is concave on the convex ambient domain. It is continuous, bounded, and positive since $s_0-a>0$. The admissible generator set $K$ excludes the maximizing point $x=0$. Declare all Borel probability measures on $K$ with fixed barycenter $\bar x=0$ feasible, with entropy per mole $\int_Ks\,dP$. For $y\in K$, define the point mass $\delta_y(A)=1$ if $y\in A$ and $0$ otherwise for every Borel set $A\subseteq K$. It is countably additive because at most one set in a disjoint family can contain $y$, and $\delta_y(K)=1$.

citations.quote:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty compact set of dimensionless generator coordinates. Each $x\in K$ labels one model-specified phase-generator state; the model assigns it entropy per mole $s(x)\in\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $s:K\to\mathbb R$ is continuous, using the numerical entropy value in that fixed unit. Define $\operatorname{conv}K$ to be the set of all finite convex combinations of points of $K$, and fix $\bar x\in\operatorname{conv}K$. Use the Borel sigma algebra relative to $K$. A Borel probability mixture is a countably additive probability measure $P$ on that sigma algebra; its barycenter and entropy per mole are the coordinatewise integrals $\int_Kx\,dP$ and $\int_Ks\,dP$. For $x\in K$, define the unit point mass $\delta_x$ by $\delta_x(A)=1$ if $x\in A$ and $\delta_x(A)=0$ otherwise, for Borel $A\subseteq K$. Assume every Borel probability mixture with barycenter $\bar x$ is feasible and has entropy per mole $\int_Ks\,dP$. Then there are $m\le d+1$, points $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in K$, and weights $\theta_i\ge0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i=1$ such that $P_*:=\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i\delta_{x_i}$ is a feasible Borel probability mixture and $\int_Ks\,dP_*\ge\int_Ks\,dP$ for every feasible mixture $P$.

Here integrals use the measure convention of [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]. The entropy map is part of the model; this theorem derives neither its microscopic meaning nor compactness of a physical phase domain.

Let $(X,\mathcal T)$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]). The
**Borel sigma-algebra of $X$** is the sigma-algebra generated by its open sets:

$$\mathcal B(X):=\sigma_X(\mathcal T).$$

Its members are the **Borel subsets** of $X$. The generated sigma-algebra exists
and is minimal by [[thm-generated-sigma-algebra-exists-and-is-minimal]].

A **probability measure** on a measurable space $(X,\mathcal A)$ is a measure $\mathbb P$ with $\mathbb P(X)=1$ ([[def-measure]]). The triple $(X,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)$ is a **probability space** ([[def-measure-space]]); $X$ is its sample space and the members of $\mathcal A$ are its events.

A measure space is a triple $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ where $\Sigma$ contains $\varnothing,X$ and is closed under complements and countable unions (a $\sigma$-algebra) of subsets of $X$ and $\mu:\Sigma\to[0,\infty]$ is countably additive with $\mu(\varnothing)=0$. A measurable function $f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]$ has measurable inverse images of Borel sets, where $[-\infty,\infty]$ has its order topology: finite open intervals and the endpoint neighborhoods $[-\infty,a)$ and $(a,\infty]$ form a basis. Its Borel sigma-algebra is generated by these open sets. A complex-valued function is measurable exactly when its finite real and imaginary parts are measurable, equivalently for the usual Borel structure of $\mathbb C$. Almost-everywhere assertions mean outside a measurable $\mu$-null set; completeness of $\mu$ is not assumed. Nonnegative extended addition uses $a+\infty=\infty+a=\infty$ for $a\in[0,\infty]$; positive scalars multiply $\infty$ to $\infty$, while $0\cdot\infty=0$. Signed expressions $\infty-\infty$ remain undefined and are not used in signed integrals. A nonnegative simple function has the form $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ with finitely many disjoint $A_j\in\Sigma$ and finite $c_j\ge0$. Define $c\mu(A)=+\infty$ if $c>0$ and $\mu(A)=+\infty$, define $0\cdot\infty:=0$, and define the finite sum of these extended nonnegative terms to be $+\infty$ if any term is $+\infty$ and otherwise the real finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]]. Then $\int s\,d\mu:=\sum_j c_j\mu(A_j)$; using canonical level sets $\{s=c\}$ makes this value representation-independent. For measurable $f\ge0$, define $\int f\,d\mu:=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: s\text{ is simple and }0\le s\le f\}$, using [[def-complete-ordered-field]] for a bounded set of finite values and setting the supremum to $+\infty$ when the values are unbounded or one is infinite. A real measurable $f$ is integrable when $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$, and then $\int f:=\int f^+-\int f^-$, where $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-:=\max(-f,0)$. Complex integrability and integration are defined by integrable real and imaginary parts.

derivations.claim: Write $w_0=P(\{0\})$ and $w_1=P(\{1\})$. By [F2], $w_0+w_1=1$ and the barycenter equation is $w_1=\tfrac12$. Hence the only feasible measure is $P_*=\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12\delta_1$.

Its entropy per mole is the finite simple-function integral
$$
\int_Ks\,dP_*=\tfrac12s(0)+\tfrac12s(1)=\tfrac12s_0+\tfrac12(s_0+a)=s_0+\frac a2.
$$
Since it is the only feasible mixture, it attains the maximum. Its two support points equal $d+1$ for $d=1$, as in [F1].

citations.quote:
Fix a working system of constitution $c$ and a closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(c)$ with equilibrium endpoints as in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. A cycle of the working system is such a record with $x_P^-=x_P^+$; the reservoirs and work store need not return to their initial energy states.

An ideal thermal reservoir $b$ has an energy interval $J_b\subseteq\mathbb R$ measured in joules and a finite entropy function $S_b:J_b\to\mathbb R$ measured in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. On the energy interval admitted for a cycle, assume the exact affine law
$
S_b(E_b)=s_{b,0}+\frac{E_b}{T_b}
$
for a constant $s_{b,0}$ and fixed $T_b>0$ kelvins. Thus $S_b'(E_b)=1/T_b$ in the interior and every admitted endpoint change is exactly $\Delta S_b=\Delta E_b/T_b$. This constant is the absolute thermodynamic temperature under [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. The affine entropy law on the admitted interval is the ideal-bath model; a finite reservoir whose temperature changes is outside this definition.

An ideal work store is a named auxiliary with an energy coordinate $E_w$ measured in joules and an assigned entropy $S_w(E_w)=s_w$ constant on the energy interval used by the cycle. It exchanges only mechanical work and no matter or heat. Its energy may change, while its entropy change is zero by this model definition.

A two-reservoir cycle contains one working-system cycle, one hot bath at $T_h$, one cold bath at $T_c$, and the ideal work store. They lie inside one isolated outer boundary in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], so the full compound has no external matter or energy transfer. There are no unlisted heat, work, matter, kinetic-energy, or external-potential-energy changes. The admitted process and transfer signs are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The model declares the endpoint entropy split
$
S_{\mathrm{tot}}=S_{\mathrm{ws}}(x_{\mathrm{ws}})+S_h(E_h)+S_{\mathrm{cold}}(E_c)+S_w(E_w),
$
where $S_{\mathrm{ws}}$ is the working-system entropy and the bath and work-store functions are those defined here. This additive constituent split is assumed to be one admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] and is the entropy supplied to [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]; $S_w$ contributes zero change. Reversibility of the full record is as in [[def-td-reversible-process]].

When the second law is applied to the cycle, the model also supplies an admitted closed process record for the full compound. At both endpoints its constituent preparations, with the declared contact controls locked or insulated, are an equilibrium macrostate for that record; its separately tracked center-of-mass kinetic and external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change. This total-compound record is the input to the second law; the working-system record $P$ is the input to its first-law balance.

In the heat-engine mode, the positive magnitudes $Q_h,Q_c$ in joules mean respectively heat taken from the hot bath into the working system and heat rejected by the working system to the cold bath; accordingly $\Delta E_h=-Q_h$, $\Delta E_c=Q_c$, $Q[P]=Q_h-Q_c$, and work output is $W_{\mathrm{out}}=-W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$. In the refrigerator mode, $Q_c>0$ is heat taken from the cold bath into the working system, $Q_h>0$ is heat rejected to the hot bath, so $\Delta E_c=-Q_c$, $\Delta E_h=Q_h$, $Q[P]=Q_c-Q_h$, and work input is $W_{\mathrm{in}}=W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$. These are idealized model conventions, not claims that a particular apparatus realizes the cycle.

For every admitted $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ with equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$, fixed material constitution, zero change in center-of-mass kinetic energy, and zero change in separately tracked external-field potential energy in the fixed chart selected by the process model, the adopted model balance is
$$U_c(x_P^+)-U_c(x_P^-)=Q[P]+W_{\mathrm{on}}[P],$$
where $U_c$ is the dimensioned energy-coordinate map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]].

Here the internal-energy coordinate is evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], while $Q[P]$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$ are the protocol transfers defined by [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], in joules as in [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The sign convention is positive $Q$ into the system and positive $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ for work done on it. If $P$ is adiabatic, its defining condition is $Q[P]=0$, so the same adopted balance gives $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]=U_c(x_P^+)-U_c(x_P^-)$.

This equation is an adopted physical postulate of the stated framework. It is not deduced here from a mechanical model or from experimental observations. Records with matter exchange or nonzero changes in omitted kinetic or external-field energy require a separately specified balance and are outside this item.

For every admitted closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ of an isolated compound, assume its declared outer boundary is isolated throughout, its material constitution is fixed, its center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change, and both endpoint preparations are equilibrium macrostates. Include every named auxiliary and work device in the compound, and restrict to constituent splits for which [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] supplies the additive total entropy. The adopted macroscopic second law is

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^+)-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^-)\ge0,$$

where $S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the sum of the constituent entropies in [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. The process record and the zero-change conditions are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The process may pass through nonequilibrium configurations; this postulate compares endpoint entropies only and assigns no entropy function to those intermediate configurations.

For an admitted reversible operation in the sense of [[def-td-reversible-process]], adopt zero total entropy change. An admitted irreversible adiabatic operation may have a strictly positive entropy increase, but strict increase is not required for every irreversible operation. The postulate does not state monotonicity for an open compound, an externally driven process, a subsystem that exchanges energy with an omitted environment, or every microscopic trajectory.

derivations.claim: The working system returns to its initial state, so $\Delta U=0$. Applying [F2] with [F1] gives $0=Q_h-Q_c-W_{\mathrm{out}}$, hence $W_{\mathrm{out}}=Q_h-Q_c$ and $\eta=1-Q_c/Q_h$.

The hot bath loses energy $Q_h$, the cold bath gains $Q_c$, and their entropy slopes are constant. Thus their entropy changes are $-Q_h/T_h$ and $Q_c/T_c$. The working system and work store have zero entropy change, so [F3] gives
$
-\frac{Q_h}{T_h}+\frac{Q_c}{T_c}=\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge0.
$
Since $Q_h,T_c,T_h>0$, step 1.2 implies $Q_c/Q_h\ge T_c/T_h$. Substituting into step 1.1 yields $\eta\le 1-T_c/T_h$. Equality in this algebraic bound holds exactly when $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=0$.
If the full admitted cycle is reversible, [F3] gives $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=0$, so step 2.1 is saturated. No converse about reversibility follows from the entropy calculation.

The process may pass through nonequilibrium configurations; this postulate compares endpoint entropies only and assigns no entropy function to those intermediate configurations.

For an admitted reversible operation in the sense of [[def-td-reversible-process]], adopt zero total entropy change. An admitted irreversible adiabatic operation may have a strictly positive entropy increase, but strict increase is not required for every irreversible operation. The postulate does not state monotonicity for an open compound, an externally driven process, a subsystem that exchanges energy with an omitted environment, or every microscopic trajectory.

derivations.claim: The working system returns to its initial state, so $\Delta U=0$. Applying [F2] with [F1] gives $0=Q_c-Q_h+W_{\mathrm{in}}$, hence $Q_h=Q_c+W_{\mathrm{in}}$.

The cold bath loses $Q_c$, the hot bath gains $Q_h$, and their entropy slopes are constant. Thus their entropy changes are $-Q_c/T_c$ and $Q_h/T_h$. The working system and work store have zero entropy change, so [F3] gives
$
-\frac{Q_c}{T_c}+\frac{Q_h}{T_h}=\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge0.
$

Since $T_c,T_h>0$, step 1.2 gives $Q_h\ge Q_cT_h/T_c$. Substituting $Q_h=Q_c+W_{\mathrm{in}}$ from step 1.1 yields
$
W_{\mathrm{in}}\ge Q_c\frac{T_h-T_c}{T_c}.
$
Divide by $W_{\mathrm{in}}>0$ and use $T_h-T_c>0$ to obtain $\mathrm{COP}_R\le T_c/(T_h-T_c)$. Equality is equivalent to $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=0$; a reversible cycle has this property by [F3].

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

Fix a material constitution $c$ and its equilibrium state domain $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Let $\Omega\subseteq D_c$ be a specified open, single-phase chart in physical SI coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, with $U$ evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame of [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. On $\Omega$, use the finite $C^2$ entropy function $S_c$ and the strict positivity $S_{c,U}>0$ adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Here $C^2$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through order two exist and are continuous ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A coordinate partial such as $S_{c,U}$ is the ordinary derivative in that coordinate direction while every other physical coordinate is held fixed, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

Define the **absolute thermodynamic temperature**, **entropic pressure**, and **molar chemical potential** of species $j$ by

$$T_c:=\frac{1}{S_{c,U}},\qquad p_c:=T_cS_{c,V},\qquad \mu_{c,j}:=-T_cS_{c,n_j}.$$

The entropy unit is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the energy $U$ is in joules, $V$ is in cubic metres, and $n_j$ is in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Thus $S_{c,U}$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $T_c$ is finite and positive in kelvins, $S_{c,V}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ and $p_c$ has units pascals, and $S_{c,n_j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\mu_{c,j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. If a microscopic model instead uses a dimensionless particle count $N_j=N_{\!A}n_j$, the corresponding per-particle chemical potential is $\mu_{c,j}/N_{\!A}$ joules, with the exact SI Avogadro constant from [[def-td-si-quantities]].

These are scalar state functions of the stated rest-frame equilibrium chart. The pressure in this definition is a derivative-defined conjugate; identifying it with force per area requires a separate adopted mechanical coupling. Neither an empirical thermometer calibration nor any equation of state is supplied by this definition.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

$$\exp(x)\to+\infty\quad(x\to+\infty),\qquad \exp(x)\to0\quad(x\to-\infty),$$
and the range of $\exp$ is contained in $(0,\infty)$ and is unbounded above with infimum $0$.

For every $\alpha>0$,
$$\lim_{x\to+\infty}\frac{\log x}{x^\alpha}=0.$$

derivations.claim: For each excited state $i\notin G:=\{i:E_i=E_0\}$, $(E_i-E_0)/(k_{\mathrm B}T)\to+\infty$, so $w_i(T)\to0$ by [F5]. Ground-state weights are $1$. Since there are finitely many states, $Z(T)\to g$, each ground-state probability tends to $1/g$, and each excited-state probability tends to $0$.

By continuity of $\log$ at $1/g>0$ from [F4], the total ground-state contribution to entropy tends to
$
-k_{\mathrm B}g\frac1g\log(1/g)=k_{\mathrm B}\log g.
$

For an excited state with $p_i(T)\to0$, set $x=1/p_i(T)\to+\infty$. By [F4], $p_i\log p_i=-\log(x)/x$, which tends to $0$ by [F6]. The finite sum of excited-state contributions therefore tends to $0$.

Combining the ground and excited contributions in the finite sum gives $S_G(T)\to k_{\mathrm B}\log g$. In the $g=1$ case this limit is $0$; for $g>1$ it is positive because $\log$ is strictly increasing and $\log1=0$.

The set of **natural numbers** is the **smallest inductive set**
([[def-inductive-set]]),

$$\mathbb{N} = \omega := \bigcap\,\{\, I : I \text{ is inductive} \,\},$$

which exists and is itself inductive by [[lem-omega-smallest-inductive]] (the
Axiom of Infinity, [[def-axiom-of-infinity]], supplies one inductive set to
intersect within, and Separation, [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]], makes the
intersection a set). On $\mathbb{N}$ we take

$$0 := \varnothing, \qquad \sigma(n) := n \cup \{n\},$$

the distinguished element and the successor function. Thus
$0 = \varnothing$, $1 = \{0\}$, $2 = \{0, 1\}$, $3 = \{0, 1, 2\}$, and in general
$n = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ is the set of its predecessors.

Equivalently (property form): if a property $P$ satisfies $P(0)$ and ($P(n) \Rightarrow P(\sigma(n))$) for all $n$, then $P(n)$ holds for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. This is the induction principle, the basis of proof by induction.

An **ordered field** is a field $F$ ([[def-field]]) together with a subset
$P \subseteq F$, the set of **positive** elements (the *positive cone*),
satisfying:

- **(O1) Trichotomy.** For each $x \in F$, exactly one of the following holds:
  $x \in P$, or $x = 0$, or $-x \in P$.
- **(O2) Closure.** If $x, y \in P$ then $x + y \in P$ and $x \cdot y \in P$.

$$a < b \;:\Longleftrightarrow\; b - a \in P, \qquad a \le b \;:\Longleftrightarrow\; a < b \text{ or } a = b.$$

$-x \in P$ (equivalently $x < 0$) is called **negative**.

derivations.claim: Let $P(N)$ mean that the endpoint after $N$ admitted operations lies in $D_+$. For $N=0$, the endpoint is the stipulated $T_{\mathrm{in}}>0$, so $P(0)$ holds.

Assume $P(N)$ [IH]. The stipulated operation sends its current temperature $T_N\in(0,T_*]$ to $rT_N$; because $0<r<1$, $0<rT_N<T_N\le T_*$, so the next endpoint satisfies $P(N+1)$. This uses the positive-temperature coordinate on the declared chart.

By [F4], steps 1.1 and 2.1 imply $P(N)$ for every finite $N\in\mathbb N$. Every admitted finite protocol has such a length by [F3], and its duration is $N\tau_*<\infty$ by the stipulated finite $\tau_*$. Since $D_+\cap D_0=\varnothing$, none reaches zero. Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an integer $n\ge1$ and an open phase-coordinate domain $O_{\rm phys}\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ with physical canonical coordinates $q_i$ in metres and $p_i$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. The canonical symplectic form on this chart is $\omega_{\rm phys}=\sum_{i=1}^n dq_i\wedge dp_i$. Let $\hat q_i=q_i/(1\,\mathrm m)$ and $\hat p_i=p_i/(1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$, and let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ be the open image of the chart in these dimensionless coordinates. The corresponding dimensionless canonical form is $\hat\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n d\hat q_i\wedge d\hat p_i$, so $\omega_{\rm phys}=(1\,\mathrm{J\,s})\hat\omega$.

Let $\hat H:O\to\mathbb R$ be a numerical energy function with continuous partial derivatives through order two, and let $H_{\rm phys}:O_{\rm phys}\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ be $H_{\rm phys}(q,p)=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat H(\hat q,\hat p)$. Where defined, its physical Hamiltonian vector field $X_{H_{\rm phys}}$ is determined by $\iota_{X_{H_{\rm phys}}}\omega_{\rm phys}=dH_{\rm phys}$. For each elapsed time $t$ in its domain, the physical flow map is a function $\phi_t:D_t\to O_{\rm phys}$, where $D_t\subseteq O_{\rm phys}$ is the set of initial data whose trajectories exist through time $t$, and it satisfies $d\phi_t/dt=X_{H_{\rm phys}}\circ\phi_t$. Equivalently, in the dimensionless chart, the flow map $\hat\phi_{\hat t}:\hat D_{\hat t}\to O$ is generated by $X_{\hat H}$ satisfying $\iota_{X_{\hat H}}\hat\omega=d\hat H$, at dimensionless time $\hat t=t/(1\,\mathrm s)$; here $\hat D_{\hat t}$ is the set of initial coordinates whose trajectories exist through $\hat t$. These definitions specify the flow maps when they exist but impose no global-existence or completeness hypothesis on the shell preparation.

A specified open interval $J_E\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular compact-shell band when $\hat H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J_E$ and $\nabla\hat H$ is nonzero at every point of $\hat H^{-1}(J_E)$.

For $\hat E\in J_E$, the energy shell is $\Sigma_{\hat E}:=\{x\in O:\hat H(x)=\hat E\}$. The graph-chart definition of the weighted shell integral is [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]: in a local graph chart $x_i=h(z,\hat E)$, its coarea measure is $d\mu_{\hat E}=dA_{\hat E}/|\nabla\hat H|$, with graph-area factor and gradient in the dimensionless Euclidean coordinates. Set $D(\hat E):=\int_{\Sigma_{\hat E}}d\mu_{\hat E}$ and admit the preparation only when $\Sigma_{\hat E}\ne\varnothing$ and $0<D(\hat E)<\infty$. Its normalized shell law is $\nu_{\hat E}(A):=D(\hat E)^{-1}\mu_{\hat E}(A\cap\Sigma_{\hat E})$. The current draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]] proves the coarea identity, chart independence and positive finite shell mass under its stated $C^2$, compact-regular-band hypotheses; its statement and proof are present, while its acceptance remains unresolved. Multiplying the unnormalized shell measure by a fixed positive phase-volume normalization does not change $\nu_{\hat E}$.

citations.quote:
**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with the
Boltzmann-constant and temperature conventions of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Declare one of the
following model readings of the same **adopted Gibbs assignment**:

(i) a fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], on its sector space,
with Gibbs generator $G:=H_N^\sigma$; or

(ii) a separately declared number-variable mode model, such as a one-mode
bosonic Fock space, a fermionic occupation space, or a declared countable
independent-mode space, with its declared assigned observables and energy
operator $H$. The model declares a self-adjoint Gibbs generator $G$ on that
space: either $G=H$, or a separately supplied self-adjoint realization of the
effective generator $G=H-\mu\mathcal N$, where $\mathcal N$ is the declared
particle-number operator and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is an assigned chemical
potential in joules. The subtraction is an operator with its supplied domain,
not an assertion that a formal unbounded difference is self-adjoint.

In either reading assume $G$ is bounded below and give its spectral PVM
$E_G$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Let $T>0$ be an assigned temperature in
kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned
Boltzmann constant $k_B$. The Gibbs assignment to either model, and the
chemical-potential identification in (ii), are additional physical
preparation assumptions made here; they are not derived from P1-P4 or from
the fixed-$N$ construction. In (ii) no restriction on the assigned real
$\mu$ is imposed beyond the declared generator and trace existence
conditions; the mode-specific convergence conditions are proved separately.
For reading (ii), $G$ specifies the Gibbs weights. If the assigned autonomous
dynamics is generated by $H$, stationarity of the Gibbs density requires its
separate dynamical or commutation hypotheses; this assignment does not
identify $H-\mu\mathcal N$ with the physical evolution generator.
The physical Helmholtz free-energy vocabulary of the entropy definition
continues to apply only to its stated nonzero finite-sector class and is not
extended to every effective generator by this postulate.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

Outside the finite-dimensional class the existence hypothesis is a genuine
restriction. For a declared non-interacting fixed-$N$ model with a supplied
countably infinite orthonormal eigenmode basis and real mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ bounded below, the complete construction and trace criterion
of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-fixed-n-countable-mode-partition-criterion]] give
$Z_N=h_N(q)$ for bosonic statistics or $Z_N=e_N(q)$ for fermionic statistics,
where $q_j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}$ and $h_N,e_N$ are the corresponding
nonnegative occupation-series sums. For every fixed $N\ge1$, either trace is
finite exactly when $\sum_jq_j<\infty$. This is a trace on the fixed-$N$
sector and permits negative mode energies.

For the separately declared full bosonic Fock models of reading (ii),
the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] and the product
criterion of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]
provide the separate mathematical full-Fock traces, with their original
positive mode-energy hypotheses: they sum over every particle number,
including the vacuum, giving $(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$ for one mode
and $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ for countably many modes.
Their physical Gibbs reading is the additional assignment of (a)(ii), not a
consequence of a mathematical trace formula. Those full-Fock traces are not
substituted for the fixed-$N$ partition trace of reading (i).

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, define its outcome law
$\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta E_A(B))$ as in
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).
If and only if the absolute first moment is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a)<\infty,$$
the model defines the **thermal mean** at temperature $T$ by
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R}a\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a),$$
read in the assigned unit $u_A$. For bounded $A$ this equals
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$. For
unbounded $A$, if the mean exists and the literal product $A\rho_\beta$ is
defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class, the mean also equals
$\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$ and
$\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho_\beta A})$; these conditional product
identities are proved by the density eigenexpansion in
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-spectral-mean-and-defined-trace-product]]. First-moment
existence alone imposes no such product or operator-square-domain condition.
When the absolute first moment is infinite the model asserts no finite
thermal mean. The identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $0<Z<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when
$Z=0$ or the partition trace diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

**(a) Adopted readings and restricted sector class.** Adopt the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], for the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. This definition
applies to the class of declared models whose sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is **finite-dimensional**, in particular to every
finite-mode realization
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]), where
$D:=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is finite (and may be zero) by
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b). Write $\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$ for the set of declared sector
preparations, that is, the density operators on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
If $D=0$, the only operator has trace zero, so
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)=\varnothing$. The partition trace is
$Z_N=0$, and there is no normalized canonical density or equilibrium free
energy; $\log D$, $D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and $\log Z_N$ are not used in this
branch. Clauses (b), (d) and (e) below apply when $D\ge1$; the assigned
parameters of (c) can still be declared when $D=0$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) Dimensionless entropy.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$
with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_D\ge0$ (counted with multiplicity, in any
order), the **entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log D],$$
the quantity of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]
clause (a) with $\log$ the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). It is dimensionless, is a function of the
eigenvalue multiset of $\rho$ alone, and equals zero exactly for pure
preparations; by clause (c) of the cited theorem $s(\rho)=\log D$ holds
exactly when $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$.

**(c) Boltzmann constant, temperature and inverse temperature.** The model
assigns a positive **Boltzmann constant** $k_B$ and a positive **temperature**
$T$; in the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the unit of $k_B$ is
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, the unit of $T$ is the kelvin, and
$$k_B=1.380\,649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$$
fixed exactly by the BIPM SI definition. The model declares the **inverse
temperature** $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$, a positive real number in $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
The value and exactness of $k_B$ are unit-convention facts; the assignment of
the parameter $T$ to a physical sample, and the identification of
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature, are adopted
assumptions of the ensemble model of this pair, not consequences of P1-P4,
and are tested identifications with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7),
whose clauses (i), (iii) and (iv) require a declared comparison and
calibration model and qualifications for measured inputs. No thermometer,
calibration or measured temperature is supplied here.

**(d) Physical entropy.** The **physical entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$S(\rho):=k_B\,s(\rho),$$
read in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$. It is nonnegative, is at most
$k_B\log D$, and vanishes exactly for pure preparations.

**(e) Free-energy functional.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$,
let $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)\in\mathbb R$ be the mean of the
declared energy observable in $\rho$ (finite because $D<\infty$, in the
moment reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).
The **Helmholtz free-energy reading** of $\rho$ is
$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$
read in joules; it is the quantity
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a)
at the identified $\beta$. For the canonical operator
$\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}/Z_N$ and
$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}\in(0,\infty)$ (positive finite sum in the
nonzero finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(f) Scope.** This definition covers only declared models with
finite-dimensional sector space, with the zero-sector branch of (a), and preparations in
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$. For a declared spatial realization, whose
sector space is infinite-dimensional, the operator $\rho\log\rho$ need not be
trace class; no entropy, physical entropy or free energy is defined here for
that case, and a separate trace-class statement would be required. The
definition asserts no increase of entropy in time, no equilibration to
$\rho_\beta$, no thermodynamic limit, no pressure or volume variable, and no
measured temperature, entropy or free energy.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $A$ be self-adjoint with regular Borel projection-valued measure $E$ from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], with $E((-\infty,a))=0$ for finite $a\in\mathbb R$. For each $\gamma>0$, define the bounded Gibbs operator $K_\gamma:=\Phi_E(f_\gamma)$ using the bounded Borel PVM integral of [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], where $f_\gamma(\lambda)=e^{-\gamma\lambda}$ for $\lambda\ge a$ and $f_\gamma(\lambda)=e^{-\gamma a}$ for $\lambda<a$. Fix $\beta>0$ and suppose $K_\beta$ is trace class in the sense of [[def-trace-class-operator]]. Then $K_\beta$ is injective and has a finite or countable orthonormal basis $(u_j)$ of $\mathcal H$ with $Au_j=E_ju_j$, $E_j\ge a$, and $K_\beta u_j=e^{-\beta E_j}u_j$. Its partition function $Z_\beta:=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta=\sum_j e^{-\beta E_j}$ is positive and finite, and $\rho_\beta:=K_\beta/Z_\beta$ is positive with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho_\beta=1$. For every $B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta B)=\sum_j(e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_\beta)\langle Bu_j,u_j\rangle$ absolutely. Further, let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be open and suppose that for every compact $C\subset J$ there is a summable family $a_j\ge0$ with $(1+|E_j|^2)e^{-\gamma E_j}\le a_j$ for all $j$ and $\gamma\in C$. Then for each $\gamma\in J$, $K_\gamma$ is trace class with partition function $Z_\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}K_\gamma=\sum_j e^{-\gamma E_j}$. With $p_j(\gamma):=e^{-\gamma E_j}/Z_\gamma$, define $\bar E_\gamma:=\sum_jp_j(\gamma)E_j$, $\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(E):=\sum_jp_j(\gamma)(E_j-\bar E_\gamma)^2$, and $S_\gamma:=-\sum_jp_j(\gamma)\log p_j(\gamma)$. These quantities are finite and satisfy $-\partial_\gamma\log Z_\gamma=\bar E_\gamma$, $\partial_\gamma^2\log Z_\gamma=\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(E)$, and $S_\gamma=\log Z_\gamma+\gamma\bar E_\gamma$ as in [[thm-tdmath-summable-canonical-differentiation]]. Countable nonnegative sums use the finite-subsum supremum convention of [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]].

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

derivations.claim: By [F1], $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ is the declared positive Gibbs weight and $\rho_\beta=K_\beta/Z_\beta$ is the model's adopted preparation. The semiboundedness, positive finite trace, AC assumptions and moment envelope in the Statement match the hypotheses of [L1].

Applying [L1] to this operator yields the finite mean and variance identities and the dimensionless spectral entropy identity $\frac{S_{\mathrm{vN}}}{k_{\mathrm B}}=\log Z_\beta+\beta\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)$. Multiplying by $k_{\mathrm B}$ and using $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$ gives $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)-T S_{\mathrm{vN}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_\beta$. The deduction is conditional on [L1] and the adopted preparation; it asserts no dynamics.

boundaries.evidence: Statement 0<Tr K_beta<infinity excludes a zero Hilbert sector or zero trace weight. Its moment envelope and normalized Gibbs density concern this nonzero physical G=H branch.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice and the canonical Gibbs-preparation assumption [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]. Restrict to its $G=H$ branch: the declared energy operator $H$ is self-adjoint, bounded below, and measured in joules; $T>0$ is in kelvins, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ has $0<Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta<\infty$. Suppose also that on an open interval $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ containing $\beta$, every compact $C\subset J_\beta$ admits a summable family $a_j\ge0$ with $(1+|E_j|^2)e^{-\gamma E_j}\le a_j$ for all energy eigenvalues $E_j$ and $\gamma\in C$. For the adopted density $\rho_\beta=K_\beta/Z_\beta$, the mean and variance of $H$ are finite and
$$-\partial_\beta\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H),\qquad \partial_\beta^2\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_\beta}(H),\qquad S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)=k_{\mathrm B}\bigl(\log Z_\beta+\beta\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)\bigr).$$
Thus $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)-T S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)$. This statement does not extend the Helmholtz interpretation to an effective generator $H-\mu\mathcal N$.
